I have been farming these 20 mu for fifty years, and with my schooling I read what the agricultural station puts out and I talk with the input dealer in town before I buy. My thinking starts from last year's books — what I spent, what I harvested — and I adjust a little each year.

I will run the wheat-maize double crop on 14 mu because that is my best flat land with good access to my well. The other 6 mu I keep in cotton — it is sandier ground, not the best for wheat, and I have grown cotton on that strip for many years. My son is off-farm so I cannot expand labor-heavy crops; cotton I manage with some hired hands at picking.

For wheat I will sow an improved Jimai-type variety, about 12.5 kg seed per mu, around October 10. I apply compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at 50 kg/mu before sowing — that gives me 7.5 kg each of N, P, K — then topdress 15 kg urea at jointing, which puts total N near 14 kg/mu. I irrigate four times: pre-sowing, overwintering if dry, jointing, and grain-filling. Two sprays usually — one for aphids and powdery mildew at heading, one earlier if weeds come heavy. I expect 520 kg/mu; last year I hit 510.

For summer maize I plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid right after wheat harvest, no-till direct seed into the stubble — saves time and keeps moisture. I put 40 kg of compound at sowing and topdress 20 kg urea at large trumpet stage, total N about 18 kg/mu. Two irrigations usually, and one spray for corn borer. Aiming for 600 kg/mu.

Cotton takes the most work and money. I use a Bt hybrid seed — bollworm is much less trouble since we switched years ago. I plough the cotton field properly in spring, apply 30 kg compound and 20 kg urea as base, then topdress 15 kg urea at flowering. I irrigate three times. Even with Bt, I still spray four or five times for aphids, spider mites, and late bollworm. I expect 270 kg seed cotton per mu.
